keyframe_review.note: 1922-1925, 1,005,709 km2: Egypt within its frontiers, with 20 edge cells along 22 N inside Sudan, 3 in Libya and 4 in Israel and 53 Egyptian cells missing (along the 25 E line, the Suez coast and the Nile valley edges), all edge effects of the 250 km2 grid. Infobox: 'Total: 3,700,000 km2' (no year, apparently with the Sudan) and '1937: 994,000 km2'; against the 1936 shape 1,005,709 the ratio is 1.01. Independence 'from the United Kingdom: 28 February 1922'.

1926-1929, 1,007,437 km2: six cells (1,500 km2) at 25 E, 23.7-26.9 N, that the 1922 and 1930 shapes lack; read as drawing noise. The page records no frontier change (it names only the 1934 cession of Sudan land to Italian Libya, which is not Egyptian).
1930-1935, 1,005,435 km2, the 1922 outline again. Infobox 'Unitary parliamentary semi-constitutional monarchy (1922-1935)'.

1936-1939, 1,005,709 km2, identical to 1922. The treaty 'required the United Kingdom to withdraw all troops from Egypt proper (excluding the Sudan)', except in the Suez Canal Zone; the outline is unchanged and the Canal Zone stays Egyptian territory with a British base, drawn by the occupation event.
1940-1943, 1,005,435 km2. The page: Egypt 'never declared war, even when the Italian Royal Army invaded Egypt'; no outline change.
1946-1947, 1,005,710 km2. The treaty page: 'In 1946, Britain agreed to withdraw all remaining troops in Egypt into the Suez Canal Zone.'

correction.text: the 1948 shape without the southern cell of the Gaza Strip: the Strip was 'under official Egyptian protection' as the All-Palestine Protectorate from 22 September 1948 and is drawn as a protectorate (lighter tint) by the ledger, not as Egyptian land

keyframe_review.note: 1948-1949, 1,005,891 km2: one cell (250 km2) at 34.36 E, 31.40 N is added to the 1946 shape (the southern Gaza Strip, Palestine in Natural Earth). The armistice of 24 February 1949 'fixed the boundaries of the Gaza Strip'; Egyptian-held Negev ground (Beersheba taken 19 May 1948) is in the contest events, not the shape.

correction.text: the 1950 shape without the southern cell of the Gaza Strip, which is the Egyptian protectorate of the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 1950-1952, 1,005,891 km2, as 1948. The page keeps the All-Palestine Protectorate under Egyptian protection until 1953 ('responsible to Republic of Egypt (1952-53)') and nominally to 1959.

correction.text: years only: the 1950-1952 outline (without Gaza) carried to 18 June 1953, when 'The Free Officers abolished the monarchy, and declared Egypt a republic'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria ends this row in 1952 and starts the Republic of Egypt in 1953; the page has the kingdom lasting under Fuad II until 18 June 1953.

region.text: Egypt: 'The United Kingdom officially recognised Egyptian independence in February 1922, abolishing the protectorate'

ledger.note: 28 February 1922: Britain recognises Egyptian independence; the Sultanate becomes the Kingdom. Infobox 'Independence from the United Kingdom: 28 February 1922' and 'Sultan Fuad I becomes King Fuad I: 15 March 1922'. The page names no land; the Cliopatria outline is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Suez Canal Zone, which Britain 'retained control of' in 1922 and kept as its base under the 1936 treaty

ledger.note: 1922: Britain keeps the Canal Zone. 'Britain retained control of the Canal Zone, the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan and Egypt's external protection' and the protection of foreigners and minorities. Troops stayed in Egypt proper until the 1936 treaty, which 'required the United Kingdom to withdraw all troops from Egypt proper' except the Zone (10,000 troops, to last 20 years) and kept Alexandria for eight years. The occupation runs past this state's end: Egypt abrogated the treaty on 15 October 1951 and the British left in June 1956 (the republic's dossier closes it).

region.text: the Negev and the coast north of Gaza where the Egyptian force fought: Beersheba occupied on 19 May 1948, Majdal the headquarters from 24 May, the advance stopped north of Isdud

ledger.note: 15 May 1948: the Egyptian army invades. 'The Egyptian force, the largest among the Arab armies, invaded from the south'; it attacked Nirim and Kfar Darom on 15 May, took Beersheba on 19 May and made Majdal its headquarters on 24 May.

region.text: the Gaza Strip, 'the All-Palestine Protectorate, which came to be called the Gaza Strip'

ledger.note: 22 September 1948: Egypt declares the All-Palestine Protectorate in Gaza. 'Egypt declared formation of the All-Palestine Protectorate on 22 September 1948'; it was 'under official Egyptian protection' with 'effective reliance upon ... Egyptian military support'. The protectorate lasts to the page's June 1959 annulment, beyond this state's end: the Republic of Egypt dossier carries the rest.

region.text: the Negev and the coast north of Gaza where the Egyptian force fought: Beersheba occupied on 19 May 1948, Majdal the headquarters from 24 May, the advance stopped north of Isdud

ledger.note: 24 February 1949: the armistice with Israel. 'the armistice of 24 February 1949' (the All-Palestine page: it 'fixed the boundaries of the Gaza Strip'); The infobox lists the 'Egyptian occupation of the Gaza Strip' as a territorial change. Israeli attacks continued to the Battle of Rafah in early January 1949.

16 October 1951: Egypt abrogates the condominium and proclaims Farouk 'King of Egypt and the Sudan'. 'On 16 October 1951, the Egyptian government abrogated the agreements underpinning the condominium'; the treaty page has it abrogated on 15 October. The Sudan stays under the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan dossier until 1 January 1956.

region.text: Egypt: 'The Free Officers abolished the monarchy, and declared Egypt a republic on 18 June 1953'

ledger.note: 18 June 1953: the monarchy ends. The Free Officers toppled Farouk on 23 July 1952, he abdicated on 26 July 1952 for Fuad II under a regency, and they declared Egypt a republic on 18 June 1953.

wars.note: Truces 11 June to 8 July and 18 July 1948. The page reads only to its first 100,000 characters here: Operation Horev, the Faluja pocket and the Sinai incursion of December 1948 were not found in the text.

notes:
Cliopatria's Kingdom of Egypt shape is modern Egypt almost without change for 31 years (3,343 to 3,344 cells); every deviation is an edge cell. Sudan (condominium with Britain), the Gaza Strip (Egyptian protectorate from 22 September 1948), the Suez Canal Zone (British base) and the Libyan frontier are the border stories, and only the second and third are drawn from this dossier.

End: Cliopatria 1952; the page gives 18 June 1953, so a keyframe kingdom-of-egypt_1953 was added; the Republic of Egypt starts 1953 in Cliopatria and may duplicate the year. Counterparts: sultanate-of-egypt (1914-1922, the predecessor; the british-africa dossier already names it as a vassal) and all-palestine-government (the Gaza protectorate 22 September 1948 to June 1959; Cliopatria's 'Palestinians' 1948 row is the West Bank, not Gaza) were written by this batch (me-10-h); republic-of-egypt (Cliopatria 1953-1957) is another part of this group. The Sudan stays with the anglo-egyptian-sudan dossier (a British colony in family britain); the condominium is not drawn as Egyptian land.

Not reached within the five-page budget: Italy's invasion in September 1940 and the Western Desert campaign (the Kingdom page says only that Egypt 'never declared war'), the 1925 Anglo-Italian settlement of the Libyan frontier (Sallum, Jaghbub), the Halaib triangle and the 1902 Sudan administrative line, the Egyptian-held Negev pockets and the Faluja pocket of 1948-49 (the war page does not name them), and the Free Officers' coup in detail. The British Canal Zone occupation has no end event because the withdrawal (completed June 1956 per the treaty page) falls after the state's end.

Gazetteer: all names (Port Said, Ismailia, Suez, Beersheba, Gaza) resolve; no unknown names.
